A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AugCLIP and the same research program. All 29 pages of v1 and 41 pages of v2, including appendices, were inspected through text and rendered pages. The material supports comparison; internal reporting inconsistencies affect specific judgments below.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-preference studies, ground-truth selection experiments, ablations, and qualitative analyses across five benchmarks, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional baseline comparisons, interpolation results, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Both retain GPT-4V attribute extraction, weighted linear classification, projection, and cosine scoring. However, v2 changes the displayed weighting formulas from averages to sums, while its new Appendix B includes image features in classifier fitting, unlike the attribute-only main-text description. The PDFs do not resolve whether these represent procedural changes or inconsistent documentation.

E1.justification: Both use CelebA, EditVal, DreamBooth, TEdBench, and MagicBrush, retaining facial-attribute, general-object, personalized-generation, object-centric, and local-editing coverage. The added analyses reuse this coverage without establishing a distinct new task or test scenario.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 3–4 add standalone SC, CLIP-I, and CLIP-T comparisons to v1 Table 2's comparator set. The interpolation study replaces directional-CLIP combinations with LPIPS, SC, DINO, and L2 by CLIP-T combinations with DINO, SC, and CLIP-I. v1's CLIPScore is retained under the name CLIPdir, and the appendix GPT-4V comparison remains.

E3.justification: The reported editing-model roster drops Plug-and-Play, MasaCtrl, and Text2Live and adds Custom Diffusion, BLIP-Diffusion, and ELITE (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 10). DreamBooth's reported size changes from 3,950 image-text pairs to 50 (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 1). Interpolation experiments also extend to ground-truth selection accuracy. These are reported setting changes; unchanged survey counts and retained scores do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The interpolation analysis is revised from directional-CLIP mixtures on three datasets to CLIP-T mixtures on five. v2 also adds qualitative comparisons of descriptions across seeds and additional directional-CLIP overmodification examples. The original weighting, attribute-count, classifier, modification-vector, and AugCLIP failure analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 and Figures 6–7 identify seeds 7, 83, 87, 88, and 94 for description examples. The five-seed experiment and reported variance of 0.0197 already appeared in v1 Appendix C.5. No increase in repeated runs or new confidence-interval or significance-testing practice is established.

E6.justification: The original AugCLIP, shared-baseline, ablation, and GPT-4V table values are retained. New comparator results materially change rankings: SC scores 0.936 against AugCLIP's 0.889 on MagicBrush, and CLIP-I ties AugCLIP at 0.857 on DreamBooth (v2 Tables 3–4). Replaced interpolation curves and additional qualitative examples add findings; they do not establish a same-setting performance improvement by AugCLIP.

T1.justification: v1 Equations 4–5 define weights through within- and between-set averages. v2 Equations 4–6 display unnormalized sums, with the within-set term excluding j=i, despite nearby averaging language. This changes the formal definition. The minimum-modification projection derivation is retained and moved from the appendix into Section 4.2.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the explicit diagnosis from directional-CLIP unreliability to context blindness across existing metrics and their combinations, and remove v1's priority claim of being first to identify the problem. The central balancing objective, five-benchmark scope, and broad human-alignment claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 develops explanations based on context blindness, MLLM attribute frequency, and SVM treatment of outlying points, and identifies simple TEdBench cases where metric interpolation can help. It removes v1's explicit warning that unreliable GPT-4V attribute extraction can distort the modification vector. Computational-cost and subjective-preference limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds algorithm pseudocode, expands and revises source/target prompting examples, and supplies the GPT-4V evaluation prompt. It revises asset listings, maps editing models to datasets, and promises release of extracted attributes. The reported 12.3-second generation and 0.15-second scoring costs were already in v1; specificity about Stable Diffusion 1.5 and noise jitter is lost.

R1.justification: v2 distinguishes Hessel's CLIPScore/CLIP-T from Gal's directional CLIP similarity and adds discussion of TIFA, GenEval, T2I-CompBench, and visual-programming evaluation. It removes citations including Rethinking FID, Pick-a-Pic, and attribute-based generative-model evaluation. The basic positioning around editing's joint preservation and modification requirements is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background, problem analysis, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Weighting precedes projection, the method is organized around two criteria, evaluation and analysis become separate sections, and the appendices are substantially reorganized with a contents page. Directional-CLIP terminology is corrected throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adds framework, geometric-explanation, and seed-example figures; redraws the motivation figure; replaces interpolation plots; and merges or relocates diagnostic examples. Combined results and ablation tables are split, the UMAP display is redrawn, and prompting and user-study layouts are rebuilt. Most original qualitative examples are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies baseline terminology, broadens comparisons, and improves navigation and explanatory detail. These gains coexist with new inconsistencies between weighting equations, prose, and Appendix B's inclusion of the scored image in classifier fitting, plus unreconciled changes in reported settings. Superiority claims also remain despite SC outperforming AugCLIP on MagicBrush. The PDFs therefore do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
